Lemma
[The Gram Determinant Formula, Pointwise]

↗ lem:gram-schmidt-preserves-orientation

If $(b_1,\ldots ,b_n)$ is a positively oriented basis of an oriented inner product space with volume form $dV$, then \[ dV(b_1,\ldots ,b_n)=\sqrt{\det (\langle b_i,b_j\rangle )}. \]

Proof

↗ lem:gram-schmidt-preserves-orientation \sketch Let $e_i$ be the oriented Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization and $A_{ij}=\langle e_i,b_j\rangle $. The Gram matrix is $A^{\mathsf T}A$, so its determinant is $(\det A)^2$. Orientation gives $\det A>0$, while the volume determinant formula gives $dV(b)=\det A$.

□
